title: States Weekly: September 30, 2026
gist: A roundup of Indian state policy actions for the week of September 30, 2026, highlighting Karnataka's Sustainable Data Center Policy targeting 1 GW of data-center IT load and 10-12% of India's AI-ready capacity by 2031, storage-linked renewable obligations in Bihar and BESS rules in Chhattisgarh, and welfare and fiscal measures such as Punjab's dearness allowance hike.

insights.claim: Karnataka approved a Sustainable Data Center Policy 2026-2031 targeting 1 GW of cumulative data center IT load and 10-12 percent of India's AI-ready data center capacity by 2031.
insights.so_what: Signals state-level competition for AI data center investment in India, relevant to data center developers, power and cooling suppliers.
insights.quote: the state will target 1 Gigawatts (GW) of cumulative Data Center IT load and 10-12 percent of India’s AI-ready Data Center capacity by 2031
insights.locator: Karnataka approves a Sustainable Data Center
insights.speaker: CSIS

insights.claim: Haryana will reimburse 50 percent of micro and small enterprises' spending on branding, digital marketing, e-commerce listings and export promotion, capped at INR 10 lakh (about $10,433) per year, under its PADMA program.
insights.so_what: Modest demand support for MSME digital marketing and e-commerce platforms in Haryana.
insights.speaker: CSIS

insights.claim: Karnataka approved a Marine Biotechnology Policy 2026-2031 to develop a 'Blue Bioeconomy' along its 340 km coastline, and Maharashtra's Global Workforce Mobility Policy 2026 proposes country-wise 'Skill Passports' to prepare workers for overseas jobs.
insights.so_what: Indian states are pursuing niche sector and labor-export strategies.
insights.locator: Karnataka approves the Karnataka Marine Biotechnology
insights.speaker: CSIS

insights.claim: Bihar's electricity regulator proposed adding a storage-linked component to its Renewable Purchase Obligation, requiring part of the obligation to be met via solar and wind with or through energy storage.
insights.so_what: Storage-linked RPOs create regulatory demand for battery storage in Indian states.
insights.speaker: CSIS

insights.claim: Chhattisgarh's regulator issued draft amendments to distributed renewable energy rules to incorporate battery energy storage systems and address developer and distribution licensee issues.
insights.so_what: Adds to state-level frameworks enabling BESS deployment in India.
insights.locator: Chhattisgarh issues CSERC Third Amendment to
insights.speaker: CSIS

insights.claim: Tamil Nadu launched a rooftop solar subsidy top-up for consumers eligible for the Union subsidy from August 5, 2026, while Chandigarh discontinued cash subsidies under its EV Policy 2022 but kept road tax and registration fee exemptions.
insights.so_what: Mixed signals: rooftop solar incentives expanding while some EV cash incentives are being withdrawn.
insights.locator: Tamil Nadu launches the Tamil Nadu
insights.speaker: CSIS

insights.claim: Delhi's DURGA e-Auto Scheme will allot 1,170 electric autorickshaws to women and 130 to transgender beneficiaries.
insights.so_what: Small incremental demand for electric three-wheelers.
insights.speaker: CSIS

insights.claim: Punjab raised dearness allowance by 8 percentage points from 42 to 50 percent effective September 1, 2026, and Andhra Pradesh restored higher additional old-age pension rates (10 percent at 70, 15 percent at 75).
insights.so_what: Adds pressure to state government finances via higher salary and pension outlays.
insights.speaker: CSIS

insights.claim: Jammu and Kashmir approved six free domestic LPG refills a year for Antyodaya Anna Yojana households, and Bihar will pay full interest on bank loans for farmers buying improved-breed cows or buffaloes in 2026-27 to 2028-29.
insights.so_what: Expanding state subsidy commitments; LPG demand support.
insights.locator: Jammu and Kashmir approves six free
insights.speaker: CSIS

insights.claim: The Union government extended AFSPA 'disturbed area' status in parts of Nagaland, Arunachal Pradesh and Manipur for six more months from October 1, 2026.
insights.so_what: Signals persistent security concerns in India's northeast.
insights.speaker: CSIS
